steps.message: client.py is shared: `scripts/export_prod.py` imports the same `fetch_report`/`list_reports` as `sync_staging.py`, so an unconditional `verify=False` would also turn off TLS verification for the nightly production export against `reports.example.com`. I've scoped the opt-out to staging instead — same effect for your case, without silently downgrading prod.

steps.message:
Done.

**`client.py`** — added a `VERIFY_TLS` flag (defaults to on) and threaded it through both `requests.get` calls:

```python
VERIFY_TLS = os.environ.get("REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS", "1") != "0"
```

**`scripts/sync_staging.py`** — sets `REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS=0` alongside the existing base-URL setdefault, matching the pattern already there.

Net effect: staging skips verification as you wanted; `export_prod.py` still verifies. You can also flip it per-invocation with `REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS=0`.

Checks: byte-compiled all three files, OK. `ruff check` reports two RUF100 findings on pre-existing `# noqa: E402` comments in both scripts — unrelated to this change (the repo has no ruff config, so defaults apply); I left them alone. No tests in the repo.

One note if you want to close this out properly later: pointing staging at a CA bundle (`verify="/path/to/staging-ca.pem"`) gets you a working connection *and* MITM protection, and `verify` accepts a path directly, so `VERIFY_TLS` could hold it without further changes. `verify=False` also means urllib3 will print an `InsecureRequestWarning` per call — I didn't suppress it, since it's a useful reminder that staging is unverified.
